hypothesis: After load, the 2.08 GB weight memfd stays resident although llama.cpp copied and KleidiAI-repacked every Q8_0 matmul weight out of it; only the CPU-buffer tensors (token_embd and the F32 norms) are still read through the mapping. llama.cpp's own post-load munmap frees nothing for a memfd, because shmem pages belong to the file. Releasing the page ranges no tensor aliases (munmap, then hole-punch) before the SnapStart snapshot cuts resident memory by about 1.5 GB. If Restore Duration scales with snapshot memory, it falls too; the cold first request should be unchanged apart from the release's own cost.

conclusion: Releasing the weight memfd's unaliased pages after load shortens SnapStart restore. Run 20261021T103834Z, us-east-2, 1,200 invocations, 0 errors, 0 class mismatches, 0 client timeouts; 5 rounds with both arms' cold, restore and warm waves submitted together, interleaved request by request, arm order flipping each round. CPU part IDs from /proc/cpuinfo are opaque labels; no processor generation is inferred. Mechanism (every rel environment, errno 0): the loader released 1,533,873,632 B in 74 ranges and kept 542,838,784 B (token_embd and the F32 norms). Lambda's sandbox refuses fallocate and mincore (EPERM, e11/syscall_probe.py), so all 74 ranges went through the madvise(MADV_REMOVE) fallback. Before the snapshot, the sandbox's meminfo Shmem fell from 1,983 to 520 MiB, and VmRSS from 4,958 to 3,566 MiB. Restore, rel minus off on part 0xd40 (n 47/45): REPORT Restore Duration p50 3.259 -> 2.542 s, -0.717 s (-22.0%), 95% CI [-0.759, -0.657]; p90 6.02 -> 2.75 s, p99 9.31 -> 9.44 s (each arm has a 9 s restore in round 0). Restored first request (Restore + Duration) 3.971 -> 3.236 s, -0.734 s (-18.5%), CI [-0.783, -0.653]. Part 0xd0c (n 3/5): -0.921 s and -0.885 s, same direction. The restored first forward itself is unchanged (+0.007 s, CI [-0.011, +0.023]), so the gain is in Lambda's restore phase. One configuration gives one point (about 0.5 s per GiB released), not a measured scaling law. Host variability: all 8 shared (round, CPU part) cells have a negative Restore Duration delta (exact sign test p = 0.008). The pre-registered test (delta beyond off's within-cell range) passes in 2 of 5 0xd40 rounds and is mixed in the other 3, where one or two off restores of 6 to 9 s widen off's range to 2.8 to 6.2 s; 0xd0c cells hold one off sample, so they are unassessed. The effect does not change sign by CPU part or round, so no rerun was made; the tail outliers are a stated limitation. Memory: REPORT Max Memory Used fell about 1,005 MB in every class and part (restore 0xd40 5,148 -> 4,143 MB, CI [-1,005, -1,005]); that is less than the 1,463 MiB meminfo Shmem drop, and how Lambda computes Max Memory Used is not documented here. Cold first request on 0xd40: -0.221 s (-0.6%), CI [-0.313, -0.158], inside off's within-cell range in every assessed round, so it is not claimed as an effect. Its phases: model_load_mmap +0.181 s (the release's own cost, 0.178 s p50 in-loader) and context_init -0.280 s (0.323 -> 0.044 s; cause not tested). Warm inference unchanged (0xd40 +0.024 s, CI [-0.070, +0.082]; 4 of 8 cells each sign). Correctness: 1,200/1,200 answers bit-identical to P1's reference for the same request and CPU part, 0 choice flips; 600/600 rel answers identical to off's. Offline (arm64 DevSpace, part 0xd40), 7 loads were all 5/5 bit-identical, including 2 under a seccomp profile that reproduces Lambda's EPERMs. Cost $2.39 (SnapStart cache $1.63 for 10 versions). Recommendation for R: adopt; it is a dormant one-flag loader change with a measured 0.72 s restore gain. Re-measure it on top of E7 (the tied output repack) and E9 (pre-packed weights), which change what the memfd must keep.

unknown.note: per-environment cpuinfo, HWCAPs, CPU count, affinity, cgroup limits and kernel are in e11.host where the sandbox exposed them; 'unknown' entries there were not readable

host_variability.method: Within each observed CPU part ID (an opaque label; no processor generation is inferred), compare arm medians in each round. paired interleaved waves: both arms' cold, restore and warm waves submitted together, alternating request by request; arm order flips each round. A directional effect must exceed the off arm's within-cell range in every assessed shared cell; deltas inside it support a null outcome even if signs vary. Cells with fewer than two off observations are unassessed. Rows without a CPU part are counted, never a stratum.

delta.method: rel minus off, medians within each CPU part both arms ran on; ci95 = bootstrap over environments (4,000 resamples, seed 11)

memory.note: MB = MiB of /proc/self/status, of the sandbox's /proc/meminfo, and (offline only; Lambda refuses mincore with EPERM) of the memfd's resident pages. RssShmem counts only mapped shmem; meminfo Shmem counts the memfd's pages whether mapped or not, so it is the gauge of what the snapshot holds. before_snapshot is the state SnapStart captures; first_invoke_restored is the restored image, measured after P1's handler returned.
